title: openai-compat: normalize tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Avery Patel
release_notes: Improve OpenAI compatibility for function/tool calling: normalize tool_choice semantics, add explicit schema mapping between Redwood tool definitions and OpenAI-style JSON Schemas, and standardize tool message formatting so streaming + tool responses are stable across SDKs and the hosted API.
description: Context: the OpenAI-compat layer currently has subtle mismatches around tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and how tool responses are surfaced in streaming mode which caused a customer-visible regression in downstream tool selection. This PR unifies behavior across the API and SDKs by (1) normalizing tool_choice to always be an object with name/confidence when provided by models that support tool_choice semantics, (2) adding a deterministic mapping layer from Redwood ToolSpecs (typed properties and examples) to OpenAI-style JSON Schema for function/tool calling, and (3) standardizing tool message formatting so streamed tool outputs emit stable assistant.tool messages followed by assistant messages representing the tool return. The change is feature-gated behind openaiCompat.toolChoiceV2 and has extensive unit and integration tests. Checklist: - add schema mapping util and unit tests - adjust openai-compat response parser to prefer tool_choice object when present - ensure streaming path emits assistant.tool messages with metadata for tooling - update docs and examples in redwood-docs - add migration notes for customers relying on legacy tool message heuristics Motivation: consistency with OpenAI semantics simplifies SDK behavior and reduces application-level parsing logic. Related Linear: ENG-2014 implements mapping and ENG-2088 covers streaming stability. See SUP-345 for customer incident that motivated this work.
commits: refactor(openai-compat): extract tool schema mapper and tests
feat(openai-compat): interpret tool_choice as object {name, confidence} when present
fix(streaming): emit assistant.tool events with tool metadata in streaming encoder
chore(docs): add migration guide and examples for tool_choice V2
test(openai-compat): add e2e test against streaming harness and mock model
ci: flake fix for tsconfig in compat package
diff_snippets:
// mapper: convert Redwood ToolSpec to JSON Schema properties
function mapToolSpecToJSONSchema(toolSpec) { return { type: 'object', properties: Object.fromEntries(toolSpec.params.map(p => [p.name, { type: p.type }])) }; }

// streaming: emit assistant.tool event with metadata
stream.emit({ role: 'assistant.tool', name: toolName, metadata: { tool_id: id, schema: schema } });
review_comments: Sasha Kim: This looks good overall. Two questions: 1) Are we confident this is non-breaking for any existing apps that depend on the old assistant message heuristics? 2) Please add a perf note about the mapper running per-tool at runtime.
Avery Patel: Added a feature flag openaiCompat.toolChoiceV2 and migration docs. The mapper is cached per-tool definition; added unit test to validate caching behavior.
Diego Martínez: Tests failed initially on CI due to a flaky example in the TypeScript harness. Added a deterministic seed for the mock model. Re-ran and all checks passed.
Priya Nair: Docs LGTM. Please include a short snippet showing how SDKs surface tool_choice in the Python example. Done.

See PR for details and migration notes.
notes_on_migration: Feature is behind openaiCompat.toolChoiceV2. Customers on hosted API will not see behavior change until opt-in or gradual rollout.
If you relied on parsing assistant messages for tool outputs, switch to SDK helpers: sdk.openaiCompat.parseToolResponse(response) which will return {toolName, payload, confidence}
Tool schema mapping may enforce stricter input validation. If you used freeform string params, update ToolSpec to include param types or mark params as type: 'string' to preserve behavior.
conversation_summary: Reviewers approved after minor test and doc fixes. Diego addressed a CI flake, and Sasha confirmed non-breaking path via feature flag and added migration docs. Merged via squash after all checks passed.
